node.title: Generic MDS residual charts have a field-independent ray bound
node.statement: Let an MDS parity-check restriction on U have rank R, |U|=R+d, and let 1<=h<=R, r=R-h. For a syndrome line with no common r-sparse support for both endpoints, if every slope in Z has an r-sparse lift supported in U, then |Z| C(d+h,d) <= C(R+d,d)R. Proof: after the trivial |Z|<=1 case, two supported slopes supply endpoint lifts; the MDS kernel restricts bijectively to every d-set T, and after cancelling T genericity leaves fewer than h persistent zeros, so every sparse slope supplies C(d+h,d) nonpersistent affine-zero charges while each (T,x) receives at most one slope. This is a fixed-chart ray theorem, not an aggregate atlas. Revised upstream PR #1106 records that the merged agreement-weighted transverse-secant theorem strictly dominates this specialization at KoalaBear, paying nullities through ten under per-witness transversality supplied by column-farness.
